create.name: Three Kingdoms Banqi: Level 7 versus Level 8, annotated
create.description: A recorded engine game, analyzed with the served Level 8 engine and pinned net. Flip choices use public pool means; reveal luck is separate. From mistboard.com/rules/three-kingdoms-banqi.

comments.text: The black chariot from h2 captures the red elephant on h1. Its 5 points take Level 7 from 95 to the winning target of 100, ending the game at 45 to 100. Seven tiles are still covered; their identities remain unknown in this study.

The black horse from g5 captures the red chariot on f3 immediately after that chariot took another black horse. The chariot is worth 15 points; Level 7 reaches 90 against Level 8’s 45. The recapture is more valuable than the 10 points just conceded.

The flip on i1 reveals the second red chariot. It provides a mobile piece, but it does not itself score points: Level 8 still trails 20 to 55. Its pool-mean expectation for this flip is 3.7%, and this chariot outcome gives 3.6%, so the draw changes little.

The red soldier on e2 takes the black chariot on e3. Three Kingdoms uses movement-based captures here, so the soldier can take the chariot. Level 8 gets its first 15 points, leaving the score 15 to 45.

The black cannon on h2 captures the red horse on e2 across the covered g2 square. The red chariot has left f2, so g2 is the only screen. The capture adds 10 points to Level 7’s total without revealing the screen’s identity.

The flip on f2 reveals a red chariot. Before the draw, the public-pool comparison prefers moving the red horse from e2 to f4 by 4.0 percentage points. The side line shows that move without using the chariot’s identity to choose it.

The black chariot captures the red cannon on g4. Level 7 has already taken the red advisor for 5 points; this cannon adds 10 and brings its total to 15. Captured-piece points, rather than the highest surviving rank, determine progress toward the win.

The opening flip reveals a red advisor on f4, giving Level 8 red ink and Level 7 black ink. Level 8’s public-pool expectation for this flip is 54.8%; the advisor outcome gives 53.7%. The draw and the choice of square are measured separately.

Level 8 has the first seat and red ink; Level 7 has the second seat and black ink. Level 7 wins on points. The graph is from the first seat. Flip grades compare public pool means, while the die marks reveal luck. Covered tiles remain unknown throughout this replay.
